latest_findings.claim: With m2 fixed at about 0.5 and e in [0, 0.9], accel_step beats force on headroom-normalized margin in both seeds: 0.40 vs 0.22 for seed 19 (accel_step R2 0.503 at L4 vs control 0.169; force R2 0.351 at L2 vs control 0.163) and 0.34 vs 0.31 for seed 18 (accel_step 0.421 vs 0.125; force 0.433 vs 0.181). But neither accel_step symbolic fit recovers a^3/r^2: seed 19 gives a^2/(r(r+1.66)) with error 0.55, and seed 18 gives a rational function of a and r/a with overall a-degree 1 and error 0.65. The force fits come out as ~1/r again (0.97/r and 1.01/r, errors 0.57 and 0.62), not 1/r^2.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Results are mixed against the pre-registered criteria. The margin prediction holds in both seeds, though narrowly in seed 18 (0.34 vs 0.31; raw margins 0.296 vs 0.252). The fit prediction fails in both seeds: no a exponent lands in [2.5, 3.5] and both errors are above 0.5. Seed 19's a^2 technically meets the expected-if-false condition (a exponent <= 2), but I do not treat that as a refutation, for three reasons. First, the fits are poor (error 0.55-0.65) and come from probe directions with R2 only 0.42-0.50. Second, a and r are strongly correlated because r lies in [a(1-e), a(1+e)], so separate a and r exponents are weakly identifiable. Third, both fitted expressions are roughly homogeneous of degree ~1 in length, which is the same overall scaling as a^3/r^2. The force fits also give r^-1 with m2 fixed, so the r^-1 seen in earlier runs is not an artefact of varying m2. Both runs completed 3000 steps and beat baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.009-0.010). Two things would change the verdict: a fit on a probe with R2 >= 0.8 (MLP or log target) that recovers a^~3 r^~-2 would support the hypothesis, and a fit that keeps r^-1 with an a exponent <= 2 would refute it.

latest_findings.claim: Refuted. With eccentricity widened to [0, 0.9] (and m2 in [0.01, 1]), the symbolic fit to the best accel_step-probe direction still comes out as r^-1 rather than r^-2 in both seeds, even though the accel_step probe beats its random control. Seed 16: 0.0103*a^2/r, fit_error_vs_true_law 0.71, accel_step R2 0.395 vs control 0.175 (margin 0.220). Seed 17: 0.00277*((a+0.685)^3/r - r), which is roughly a^3 but still r^-1, fit_error 0.62, accel_step R2 0.503 vs control 0.182 (margin 0.321). Accel_step beats force in both seeds: force R2 0.154 vs control 0.057 (margin 0.097, fails the 0.1 threshold) and 0.237 vs control 0.131 (margin 0.106). The force fits were m2/r + 0.40 and (m2 + 0.60)/r, errors 0.90 and 0.64. Prediction stays strong: val_mse_ratio 0.0137 and 0.0128.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds meet the expected-if-false criteria on their own: accel_step margin >= 0.1, r exponent about -1, fit error >= 0.3. Seed 16 also has an a exponent of 2. The main caveat is that the accel_step probe direction explains only 40-50% of accel_step variance at e <= 0.9, down from 0.92-0.95 at e <= 0.5. So the symbolic fit describes a weak linear approximation. The r^-1 result could come from a linear probe failing to follow the heavy-tailed 1/r^2 near pericentre, rather than from the model encoding an r^-1 quantity. Three things would flip this to inconclusive or supported: (1) an MLP probe or a log(accel_step) probe reaches R2 >= 0.8 and its fitted direction gives r^-2; (2) fits restricted to systems in a narrow band of a give r^-2; (3) further seeds recover r^-2. Data seed 0 is shared by both runs, and probing was final-only.

latest_findings.claim: Fixing m2 at 0.5, so that force is exactly 0.5/r^2, did not lift the force probe. Final force R2 was 0.750 at layer 1 (seed 14, control 0.560, margin 0.19) and 0.732 at layer 2 (seed 15, control 0.508, margin 0.224). accel_step reached 0.924 and 0.946 at layer 4 (controls 0.743 and 0.762, margins 0.18), a raw R2 lead of 0.17-0.21 over force. Distance was decoded at 0.87-0.89, so the force ceiling of about 0.73-0.75 comes from the 1/r^2 nonlinearity or how the layers encode it, not from m2 information missing from the residual stream.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds independently meet every expected-if-false criterion by a wide margin: force R2 is at most 0.78 (0.75 and 0.73, inside the 0.65-0.74 band from spread-m2 runs), and accel_step leads by at least 0.12 (0.175 and 0.215). Neither seed approaches the 0.85 force R2 the hypothesis predicted. The main limit is that both runs stopped before 3000 steps. Seed 14 stopped at step 1500 (val_mse_ratio 0.063) and seed 15 at step 2500 (0.0145). The later, better-trained seed has the slightly lower force R2, so more training is unlikely to close a gap of more than 0.1, but this is not proven. Only linear probes were used. A nonlinear or log-target probe that decodes force at 0.85 or higher with m2 fixed would show the ceiling is a linear-readout artifact rather than a representational one, though it would still not support the m2 hypothesis. A full 3000-step run showing force R2 at 0.85 or above would reopen the question.

latest_findings.claim: The pre-registered refutation condition was met: in seed 12 the fitted accel_step direction scales as a^2/r (r exponent -1), not a^3/r^2. Neither seed met the success criteria, since both fits scale as a^2 rather than a^3 and both fit errors exceed 0.2 (seed 12: 0.202, seed 13: 0.233). Seed 13's fit, a^2*0.0113/(m2*r^2 + r), runs between r^-1 (small m2) and r^-2 (m2 near 1). Both runs finished all 3000 steps (val_mse_ratio 0.015 / 0.017). The accel_step probe clearly beats control (R2 0.917 / 0.883 vs control 0.738 / 0.674, margins 0.179 / 0.210, layer 4). The force probe has the larger margin (R2 0.707 / 0.712 vs control 0.451 / 0.468, margins 0.257 / 0.243, layers 1-2). As the hypothesis predicted, the force-direction fit does not recover m2/r^2: it gives (m2 + 0.24)/r and (m2 + 0.26)/r, with fit errors 0.41 / 0.39.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The verdict rests on the pre-registered clause 'at least one seed keeps an r exponent near -1', which seed 12 meets cleanly. Seed 13 is in between: its r exponent depends on m2 and its fit error of 0.233 is between the true (<0.2) and false (>=0.3) thresholds, so the two seeds do not independently agree. One major caveat: with eccentricity in [0, 0.5], r stays within a factor of about 1.5-3 of a. That makes a^3/r^2, a^2/r and a nearly collinear, so symbolic regression may not be able to tell these forms apart. 'a^2/r instead of a^3/r^2' may therefore reflect an identifiability limit of the data rather than a different learned law. Both probe margins clearly beat control in both seeds, so some gravity-like structure is there; what is in doubt is its exact form. The verdict would weaken toward inconclusive or flip to supported if fits on data where r and a are decorrelated (eccentricity up to 0.9, or per-snapshot fits at fixed a) recovered r^-2 with a^3 in both seeds. It would strengthen if r^-1 persisted under those conditions.

latest_findings.claim: Once training covers e in [0, 0.8], the high-eccentricity gap is gone in both seeds. On held-out high-e systems val_mse_ratio is 0.0187 (seed 9) and 0.0189 (seed 8), about 1.05x and 1.01x the in-distribution 0.0178 and 0.0187, and no worse than held-out low-e (0.0185, 0.0215). The probes still beat their random controls at the last checkpoint: force margin 0.208 (R2 0.452 vs control 0.244, layer 4) and 0.312 (0.528 vs 0.216, layer 1); accel_step margin 0.337 (0.715 vs 0.378) and 0.358 (0.707 vs 0.349), both at layer 4. accel_step has the larger margin over its control than force in both seeds.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds clearly meet the expected-if-true criteria: the high-e/in-distribution ratio is about 1.0x against a 3x threshold, and every probe margin is at least 0.2 against a 0.1 threshold. Three things limit confidence. (1) Both runs stopped at step 2500 of 3000 after using only 0.13 of the 0.2 h budget, and val_mse_ratio was still falling (0.034 to 0.018 over the last 500 steps). The 'final' checkpoint is therefore step 2500 and the models had not converged. Stopping early should not reverse a 1x vs 3x result, but it is unexplained. (2) This shows the earlier 16-18x gap was a coverage gap in prediction. It does not show the internal representation works equally well at high e: the best force probe R2 on held-out high-e is only 0.366-0.377, against 0.729-0.802 on held-out low-e, while prediction error is the same on both. That repeats the earlier drop to 0.34-0.40, and there is no random control on the eval sets, so this probe drop is not explained. (3) Two seeds, one data seed, one architecture (L=4, d=64, N=64). The verdict would weaken if training to 3000 steps or a further seed opened a high-e gap above 3x, or if an OOD random control showed the force probe does not beat chance on high-e systems.
